title: test-0013-SCI-CHM-ATOMSTRUCT
passage: In our science lab today, we explored the structure of the atom using a simulation of Rutherford’s famous gold foil experiment. We observed that most alpha particles passed straight through the thin gold sheet, proving that the atom is mostly empty space, not filled with air or solid matter. A few particles were deflected at large angles, which showed that the positive charge is concentrated in a tiny, dense nucleus at the center, rather than being a spread-out fluid or jelly. We also learned that electrons are not stationary seeds stuck in a solid sphere; instead, they move rapidly in defined energy levels around the nucleus. These shells are not physical walls or containers but regions of space where electrons are likely to be found. Furthermore, we discussed that the mass of an atom is concentrated in the nucleus, where protons and neutrons reside. While protons are positively charged, neutrons are neutral, meaning they carry no charge at all. Finally, we noted that isotopes are simply atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons, not entirely new elements. This experiment helps us visualize the atom as a dynamic system rather than a static, solid object.
summary: We saw that most alpha particles went straight through a thin gold sheet, showing that the atom is mostly empty space, not filled with air or matter. Furthermore, we discussed that the mass of an atom is concentrated in the nucleus, where protons and neutrons reside.
